subject: Telemetry anomaly: request for IR artifacts, access, and customer notification plan
messages:
From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>
To: Ava Morgan <ava.morgan@finori.co>, security@finori.co
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 10 Sep 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Telemetry anomaly: request for IR artifacts, access, and customer notification plan

Hi Ava / Finori security team —

We observed an unusual spike in downstream telemetry for your tenant (org-id: finori-prod-43) beginning ~2026-09-09T22:40Z and continuing in short bursts through last night. Token throughput to a small subset of model shards increased ~18x for ~35-minute windows; we also see a handful of requests with malformed prompt headers that triggered our validation fallback. No exfiltration indicators (S3 egress, external IP data flows) are present in the routes we control.

Out of an abundance of caution we want to share the incident artifacts we have and align on a short IRP handoff so you can perform any additional forensic work on your side. Attached are: a trimmed telemetry CSV with the anomalous sessions (telemetry_snippet_20260910.csv), the audit log extract from our access plane (audit_log_extract_20260910.txt), and an internal action matrix draft (ir_action_matrix_v1.pdf) that lists our containment steps and proposed timeline.

Requests / asks:
- Please confirm whether Finori has observed related alerts on your API gateway or WAF for the same windows.
- If you want us to open a shared, read-only S3 bucket for raw traces and full logs, tell us the destination bucket ARN and a preferred TTL for objects.
- Can we schedule a 30-minute call today to align next steps and customer-facing notification language? We propose 14:00 PT / 17:00 ET but are flexible.

Short summary of steps we've already taken:
- Isolated the affected serving pool and applied an emergency token-limit rule to prevent burst replays.
- Rolled a transient routing change to force new sessions through the validated path.
- Snapshot of KV caches and GPU job metadata saved to immutable storage.

If you prefer a go-forward coordination model (Redwood collects artifacts + Finori owns cross-tenant analysis + AuditBridge engaged), cc James O'Neill at AuditBridge and we'll proceed.

Thanks — we'll keep this thread as the single source of truth for the artifacts.

—
Soojín Lee
Senior Security Engineer, Redwood Inference
soojin.lee@redwood.ai
+1 415-555-0123

Attachments: telemetry_snippet_20260910.csv (CSV, trimmed), audit_log_extract_20260910.txt (TXT, redacted), ir_action_matrix_v1.pdf (PDF, internal)

From: Ava Morgan <ava.morgan@finori.co>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>
Cc: security@finori.co, James O'Neill <j.oneill@auditbridge.com>
Date: Thu, 10 Sep 2026 10:03:00 -04:00
Subject: Re: Telemetry anomaly: request for IR artifacts, access, and customer notification plan

Hi Soojin —

Thanks for the quick heads-up and for the artifacts. We see matching alert signatures on our API gateway (spikes from 22:38–23:15Z) and intermittent 429s in the same windows. We have Security Ops standing up a triage runbook now.

A few quick answers:
- Please provision a read-only S3 bucket to arn:aws:s3:::finori-redwood-ir-readonly and set TTL to 90 days. Our security ops can grant AuditBridge access after you upload.
- We'd like to avoid a broad customer notification for now. Can you share a short, plain-language incident blurb we can adapt for internal comms? If the investigation changes, we'll follow your recommended notification cadence.
- 17:00 ET works for a quick sync; I've looped James from AuditBridge in case we need a vendor-led forensic assist.

Also, do you have a sanitized sample of the malformed prompts? We want to confirm whether any PII-like patterns triggered the validation fallback.

Best,
Ava Morgan
Head of Security, Finori
ava.morgan@finori.co

Hi Ava —

Thanks for the quick reply and the S3 details; we'll upload the full extracts to the bucket you provided and share pre-signed links with the Finori security team and AuditBridge once the transfer completes.

To address your asks:
- Sanitized prompt samples: attached (sanitized_prompts_samples.txt). We removed any tokenized content and scrubbed obvious patterns; the samples show repeated malformed header markers and unusual repeat tokens (example: "<[X-UNK]>...<REPEAT-SEQ>").
- Short incident blurb (internal-facing) is below — feel free to adapt: 
  "Redwood detected an unusual traffic pattern to Finori's tenant that resulted in elevated request rates to a small subset of model shards. No evidence of data exfiltration from Redwood-managed routes has been found. Redwood and Finori security teams are coordinating for further analysis; artifacts have been shared with AuditBridge for forensic review."

Proposed timeline:
- Today (09/10): upload artifacts; 17:00 ET sync for triage and next-step alignment.
- 09/11: forensic deep-dive (AuditBridge) + decision on customer notification by 18:00 ET.
- 09/14: preliminary postmortem draft shared.

We attached an updated action matrix where we list the responsible owners for each containment and evidence task (ir_action_matrix_v1.pdf). Karthik and Ben will drive telemetry export and logs redaction respectively.

—
Marissa Cole
Head of Incident Response, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai

Attachments: sanitized_prompts_samples.txt (TXT, sanitized)
